answers.answer: Give each player a Clover board and marker; shuffle the Keyword cards into a face-down deck within everyone’s reach. Each player draws 4 cards and places them randomly in the board’s recessed spots, hidden from the other players.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Shuffle the Keyword cards into a face-down deck”; “draws 4 Keyword cards” and places them “randomly”; “Keep your cards hidden.”

answers.answer: The phases are Choosing Clues, then Resolution. In Choosing Clues, everyone works individually, simultaneously, and secretly. The two Keywords below each Clue Zone form a Pair, making four Pairs.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Choosing Clues: everyone works individually, simultaneously and secretly,” followed by “Resolution.” Actions: “The 2 Keywords below each Clue Zone form a Pair: there are four Pairs.”

answers.answer: A Clue must be a single word; compound words are allowed. It may be a common noun, proper noun, acronym, number, or onomatopoeia.
answers.evidence: Actions: “A Clue must be a single word; compound words are allowed,” followed by the five forms: “common noun, proper noun, acronym, number or onomatopoeia.”

answers.answer: No. A Clue cannot be either Keyword itself.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: “Either Keyword itself, or its translation into another language.”

answers.answer: No. Amour is a translation of Love, and a Clue cannot be a Keyword’s translation into another language.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues gives the example: “Amour cannot connect Love and France.”

answers.answer: No. Prince is in the same word family as Princess, which is an invalid Clue.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: “A word in the same family as a Keyword: Prince cannot connect Princess and Brother.”

answers.answer: No. Cuppajo is made up, and made-up words are invalid Clues.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: “A made-up word: Cuppajo cannot connect Mug and Morning.”

answers.answer: Each player writes 4 Clues, one connecting both Keywords in each Pair, in the corresponding Clue Zone.
answers.evidence: Actions: “For each Pair, write one Clue connecting both Keywords in the corresponding Clue Zone. Write 4 Clues in total.”

answers.answer: Remove all four Keyword cards from the board, draw 1 new card without looking at it, shuffle it with the four removed cards, then put the board down with the five cards in a face-down pile on top.
answers.evidence: After writing all four Clues: “Remove all four Keyword cards”; “Draw 1 new card without looking at it, and shuffle it with those four cards”; put the board down with “the 5 cards in a face-down pile on top.”

answers.answer: Resolution starts only after everyone has finished the preparation steps.
answers.evidence: “Start Resolution only after everyone has finished these steps.”

answers.answer: The first Spectator is chosen when Resolution begins; the summary does not specify a selection method. The other players look at the Spectator’s board and work together to reconstruct its original Pairs using the written Clues. The Spectator may not communicate in any way, including speech, hints, or gestures.
answers.evidence: “Choose the first Spectator when Resolution begins.” The other players “work together to reconstruct” using the Clues; the Spectator “cannot communicate in any way,” including “speech, hints or gestures.”

answers.answer: The Spectator reveals their Clover board and all 5 cards face up in the middle of the table. The others try to put the four original cards into the correct spaces and orientations on the board, leaving the extra card off it.
answers.evidence: Resolution and verification: the Spectator puts “their Clover board and all 5 cards face up in the middle”; others reconstruct the original Pairs, placing four original cards correctly and “leaving the extra card off it.”

answers.answer: The player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.
answers.evidence: “If they disagree about placement, the player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.”

answers.answer: Yes. Guessers may discuss their reasoning and physically try arrangements. The Spectator verifies once they agree on a placement.
answers.evidence: “The guessers may discuss their reasoning and physically try card arrangements”; “Once they agree on a placement, the Spectator verifies it.”

answers.answer: They score 6 points: 1 point per card (4) plus a 2-point first-try bonus. No second attempt is needed.
answers.evidence: “First attempt, all Pairs correct: score 6 points: 1 per card (4) plus a 2-point first-try bonus. The board is resolved; no second attempt is needed.”

answers.answer: The Spectator silently removes the incorrect card(s) and puts them in the middle of the table. They may not explain the mistake or otherwise communicate; the team receives a second and final attempt.
answers.evidence: On a first-attempt error, the Spectator “silently removes the incorrect card(s)” and puts them “in the middle of the table”; the others get “a second and final attempt.” Special Rules: the Spectator “may not explain the mistake or otherwise communicate.”

answers.answer: The score is 4 points, one per correct card, with no first-try bonus.
answers.evidence: Second attempt: score “1 point per correct card remaining,” for “0–4 points, with no first-try bonus.” Special Rules: a second-attempt perfect board is worth “4, not 6.”

answers.answer: The Spectator removes the wrong card to the middle of the table. The team scores 3 points, one per correct card remaining, and there is no third attempt.
answers.evidence: “After resolving” on the second attempt, the Spectator removes “any incorrect cards to the middle of the table.” Score is “1 point per correct card remaining”; “There is no third attempt.”

answers.answer: The Spectator turns the board over and writes its points in the middle, discards all 5 used Keyword cards, and the player to their left becomes the next Spectator.
answers.evidence: “The Spectator turns it over, writes its points in the middle, and discards all 5 used Keyword cards. The player to their left becomes the next Spectator.”

answers.answer: The game ends after every player has been Spectator once; each player is Spectator exactly once. Add the points written on the boards, record the team total in the Record of Legends, and try to beat the previous high score.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player is Spectator exactly once per game.” Scoring: “After every player has been Spectator once, the game ends”; add all points, “record the team total in the Record of Legends,” and “try to beat your previous high score.”
